company: Golden Rim Resources Ltd (ASX: GMR, now trading as AS1)
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Any person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities including any director (Key Management Personnel); any employee of the Group; any contractor nominated by the Board as a person to whom the policy applies; and any Connected Person of the foregoing. All substantive restrictions (Blackout Periods, prior written clearance for every trade, hedging and margin loan clearance requirements) apply uniformly to this tier; only the Approving Officer differs.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons (other than the Chair)
tiers.description: All Restricted Persons except the Chair; distinguished only for clearance, which is given by the Managing Director (or, if the Managing Director is the applicant, by the named alternate Kathryn Davies), with the Chair as alternate approver.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: A Restricted Person distinguished only for clearance: the Board is the Approving Officer for the Chair, with no alternate.

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: A Restricted Person's spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18, a parent, an unlisted body corporate of which the Restricted Person is a director, a trust of which the Restricted Person is trustee and beneficiary (or of which a listed relative is beneficiary), or any other person over whom the Restricted Person has significant influence or control. Is itself a Restricted Person; the Restricted Person must take all reasonable steps to procure the Connected Person's compliance.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding in the Company

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release to ASX of the Company's quarterly report (March, June, September or December quarter)
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the quarterly report

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may from time to time declare an Additional Period during which trading is prohibited (for example because the Company is considering matters that would require disclosure but for Listing Rule 3.1A). You must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.

rules.detail: Securities is defined to include 'derivatives of any of the aforementioned' (shares, share acquisition rights, options, debentures) with no venue limitation, so an OTC put/call is a Security. Section 6 requires prior written clearance before trading in Securities at any time, not merely during Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: Securities are securities issued by the Company and include shares, share acquisition rights, options, debentures (including bonds and notes) and derivatives of any of the aforementioned.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on transactions or arrangements that limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging transactions over vested shares (the Policy does not separately address a holding-lock state) require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer; no outright ban applies once vested.
rules.evidence: Before entering into any transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding in the Company you must first obtain prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Not named; a prepaid forward or similar structure limits the economic risk of the underlying holding and so falls within the unvested hedging ban.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Caught only as a transaction that operates to limit economic risk (the hedging clause) or as an agreement to dispose of Securities; requires prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: Before entering into any transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding in the Company you must first obtain prior written clearance.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named. A CFD referencing the Company's shares is a derivative Security requiring ordinary prior written clearance, or is caught as hedging under 8.1 if it operates to limit economic risk.
rules.evidence: Securities ... include shares, share acquisition rights, options, debentures (including bonds and notes) and derivatives of any of the aforementioned.

rules.detail: Margin loans are named expressly and are not banned; they require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer, with no vesting-state distinction.
rules.evidence: You must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: The margin loan clause extends to 'other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities' generally, covering any grant of security over Securities as collateral, subject to prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: You must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.

rules.detail: Unlike many comparable policies, secured financing against Securities is not banned; it is expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer, with no restriction to margin-lender products specifically.
rules.evidence: other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no short-term or speculative trading restriction, unlike many comparable policies.

clearance.approver: Managing Director (or, if the Managing Director is the applicant, Kathryn Davies); Chair as alternate
clearance.evidence: You must not trade in Securities at any time ... unless you first obtain prior written clearance from: Restricted Person other than the Chair - Approving Officer: Managing Director and in the case of the Managing Director, Kathryn Davies; Approving Officer alternate: Chair. ... Any written clearance ... will be valid for the period determined by the Approving Officer, which period will usually be 5 business days from the date that the clearance is given.
Chair - Approving Officer: Board; Approving Officer alternate: n/a.

exceptions.evidence: You may be in severe financial hardship if you have a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant Securities.

A circumstance may be considered exceptional if you are required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell, or accept a transfer of, Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for you to do so.
a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
acceptance of a takeover offer or participation in a scheme of arrangement.

exceptions.approver: Board (approves timing and structure of the offer)
exceptions.evidence: trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
the exercise or automatic conversion of options or other convertible rights issued under an employee incentive scheme (but not the disposal of the underlying share following exercise or conversion).

an acquisition, or agreement to acquire, or grants, allocations or vesting of shares, rights or awards under an employee incentive scheme (including the Company's Director and Employee Remuneration Plan) (but not the disposal of the underlying share following exercise or conversion).
an issue of Securities to a director, which has been approved by shareholders.

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Securities by that trust provided that the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person.

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy and where: (i) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; and (ii) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.

transfers of Securities between a Restricted Person and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child, family company, family trust or other close family member or of Securities already held in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary.

exemption_authority: The relevant Approving Officer may, in their sole and absolute discretion, grant prior written clearance to trade during a Prohibited Period for severe financial hardship or other circumstances they deem exceptional (including a court order or overriding legal/regulatory requirement), provided the applicant is not in possession of Inside Information.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loans permitted with clearance, not banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many comparable ASX policies that ban margin lending/secured financing outright, this Policy merely requires clearance, materially improving the prospects for a funded-collar loan secured on the Restricted Person's shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call is expressly excluded from the trading restrictions (including the Blackout Period regime) and needs no fresh clearance, materially de-risking enforcement mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested entitlements
bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The absolute hedging ban only bites on unvested equity remuneration; a collar over vested, unencumbered shares needs only ordinary clearance under 8.1, not an outright bar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary will maintain a register of clearances given in accordance with this section 7, and must report all clearances given to the Board at its next following meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no explicit personal obligation on the Restricted Person to notify the Company Secretary after dealing; any director-level ASX/Corporations Act notification obligations apply independently of this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no clause restricting short-term or speculative dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no minimum holding period or anti-speculation objection that could otherwise constrain the tenor of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clauses 4 and 5 (Blackout period; Exceptional circumstances) cross-reference 'the procedure for prior written clearance described in section 7', while the clearance procedure is itself headed as section 6 and the exceptions list as section 7.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Likely a drafting artefact from renumbering; it does not change the substantive rule that clearance must always be sought before trading, including during a Prohibited Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This document is a 13 July 2020 ASX announcement by Golden Rim Resources Ltd (ASX: GMR), the entity that appears to now trade as AS1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As the only policy text available it has been extracted in full, but its age and the apparent company rename/ticker change warrant confirming the current policy in force before relying on this analysis.

summary: A funded collar is comparatively achievable under this policy, once vested. The hedging clause (8.1) bans only transactions limiting the economic risk of unvested equity remuneration outright; over vested shares, both the hedging clause and the margin loan/secured lending clause (8.2) merely require prior written clearance from the Managing Director (or the Board for the Chair), not an outright prohibition, so the put/call legs and the secured loan leg are each structurally permitted subject to clearance. All trading, whether inside or outside a Blackout Period, requires prior written clearance in any event, and must avoid the quarterly Blackout Periods and any Board-declared confidential Additional Period unless exceptional circumstances clearance is obtained (which, unusually, is not limited to sales only). A lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the restrictions altogether, materially de-risking the bank's security enforcement. There is no short-term trading restriction and no minimum shareholding requirement to navigate. Overall, subject to obtaining the required clearances for both legs and timing execution around Blackout Periods, this policy is one of the more collar-friendly reviewed.
